title: The Service Story Catalog has no epic-level scope or suggested-owner column
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Catalog v1.xlsx (Epics sheet columns: Epic, Name, Stories, Lanes, Day-1 stories, Wave); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx (Services sheet); Template and Rules v1 §R5.1, §R5.2, §R5.3 and U3
section: §1, §2 and §3-§5 (scope and suggested owner per epic); §6 (Day-1 work by team type)
description: The catalog holds the suggested owner per story (1034 rows) and the Ownership Map holds service ownership per table, API operation, event, workflow and job, but neither holds an owner or a scope for the 31 epics, and no source states how the per-story owner is reduced to one owner per epic. The epic scope appears only inside the epic ID (RWB-SVC-P1, RWB-PLT-LIB, RWB-ITG-W2). An epic file that states a scope and an owner per epic therefore derives both values.
evidence: Catalog Epics sheet has six columns and no owner or scope column; Catalog Stories sheet column 'Suggested owner' carries the fixed phrases of §R5.3; Ownership Map Services sheet has Code, Service, Name, Wave, Schema, REST base, Topic, Queue and no owner column; §R5.2 gives the scope tokens PLT, ITG, P1-P10 and S1-S9 inside the story and epic ID; §R5.3 gives the owner phrase per work type
proposed: Keep the epic owner as the derived suggestion recorded here, or add a Scope and an Owner column to the Service Story Catalog Epics sheet in a later version so the value is stored rather than derived

title: The epic wave is not defined for an epic whose stories span several business-epic waves
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Catalog v1.xlsx (Epics sheet Wave; Stories sheet Wave); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx (Services sheet Wave); Template and Rules v1 §R5.6
section: §1, §2 and §4 (epic wave and Arch v5 wave); §7 (epics per wave)
description: A service epic holds stories of several business epics, and a story keeps its W-MAP wave when that is earlier than the service's Arch v5 wave (§R5.6), so the stories of one epic carry different waves. The catalog shows one wave per epic but does not state the rule behind it: reading the story waves back gives the earliest wave for all 31 epics, while the service's Arch v5 wave is later for seven of them (S3, S4, S5, S6, S8, S9 and P8). The same table in §R5.6 puts 'Platform and NF' at wave 0, while the epic RWB-ITG-NFR is at wave 1 because its two stories are wave-1 EP01-TE stories and not NF-01 to NF-08.
evidence: Epics sheet wave 2 for RWB-SVC-S3 against Ownership Map wave 3 for rwb-guarantee; the same for S4 (2 / 3), S5 (1 / 2), S6 (3 / 4), S8 (1 / 2), S9 (1 / 4) and P8 (1 / 2); Stories sheet: RWB-SVC-S7 spans one wave (4) while RWB-SVC-P1 spans waves 1 to 4; §R5.6 W-MAP table row 'Platform and NF | 0'; RWB-ITG-NFR holds RWB-ITG-TE009-ITG and RWB-ITG-TE010-ITG at wave 1 with tag EP01-TE, while the NF-01 to NF-08 stories sit in the platform epics at wave 0
proposed: State the epic-wave rule in the next version of Template and Rules §R5.6 (epic wave = earliest wave among its stories, with the service wave shown beside it) and use the word NF only for the NF-01 to NF-08 stories

title: Epic lane counts add to 547 while the programme has 510 distinct lanes
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Catalog v1.xlsx (Epics sheet Lanes; Stories sheet Lane); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json stats (lanes 510)
section: §2 (lanes per epic); §8 (lanes and contract groups); §9 (totals and reconciliation)
description: The Epics sheet counts the lanes of each epic, but a contract group CG-W<n> is one lane shared by every epic of its wave, so the per-epic column adds to 547 while the programme has 510 distinct lane IDs. Neither the catalog Read me nor the rules document states which convention the Lanes column uses, so an epic file that repeats the numbers has to explain the difference.
evidence: Sum of the Epics sheet Lanes column = 547; distinct values in the Stories sheet Lane column = 510; split_plan.json stats.lanes = 510; CG-W4 alone appears in 92 stories across 10 epics; CG-W0 in 17 stories across 4 epics
proposed: Add a note to the Service Story Catalog Read me that the Lanes column counts a shared contract group once per epic, and keep both numbers in the epic overview
